THROAT SYMPTOMS

Assess the patient with throat symptoms not needing urgent attention • Ask about swallowing problems. If food/liquid gets stuck with swallowing, refer. • If difficulty or pain on swallowing, with white patches on cheeks/gums/tongue/palate, oesophageal candida likely 52. • Wear a mask while examining the throat. Check for redness, grey membrane, bleeding and white patches.
Is there sore throat and a thick grey layer (pseudomembrane) in throat/nose, with or without mild fever?

Red throat and/ or swollen tonsils, tender neck lymph nodes, cough, runny
nose
Consider diphtheria • Protect yourself from occupational exposure 196. • Isolate patient. While awaiting transport: - Monitor pulse, BP and oxygen saturation. If oxygen saturation < 94%, give
oxygen3 to keep saturation ≥ 94%. - If airway obstruction (snoring, gurgling, noisy breathing), assess airway 16. - Give single dose azithromycin 500mg. If unable to swallow, give instead single

dose aqueous benzyl penicillin 25000IU/kg IV, up to 1MIU. • Discuss diphtheria antitoxin (DAT) with NICD hotline 200. • Alert lab and send swab according to NICD guidance. • Notify4 within 24 hours. • Identify close contacts and discuss with provincial CDC5 directorate. • Refer.
Viral tonsillopharyngitis
likely Explain that antibiotics are not

Bacterial tonsillopharyngitis likely • May also have generalised red rash, red spots in back of throat or a red tongue with bumps (strawberry tongue). • If ≤ 21 years old, give one of: - single dose of benzathine benzylpenicillin
1.2MU IM2 or - amoxicillin 1g 12 hourly for 10 days or - phenoxymethylpenicillin 500mg 12 hourly
for 10 days. - If severe penicillin allergy (history of anaphylaxis,

urticaria or angioedema), give instead azithromycin 500mg daily for 3 days. • If > 21 years old, advise to return if symptoms persist/worsen: discuss/refer. • If ≥ 6 episodes per year, refer for ENT assessment.

• Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Advise to gargle with salt water for 1 minute twice a day (Add ½ teaspoon of table salt to 200mL lukewarm water). • Advise to avoid spicy, hot, sticky, dry or acidic food and to eat soft, moist food. Keep hydrated.

1Common allergens include medication, food or insect bite/sting within the past few hours. 2Dissolve benzathine benzylpenicillin 1.2MU in 3.2mL lidocaine 1% without adrenaline (epinephrine). 3Give 1-4L/min via nasal prongs or 6-10L/min via facemask (up to 10-15L/min via non-rebreather mask). 4Notify within 24 hours via NMC App (download from NICD website/app store) or www.nicd.ac.za/nmc-overview/notification-process. 5CDC = Communicable Disease Control.
